annotations.text: Yale's weighted_etr is an EFFECTIVE statutory rate (post mutual-exclusion stacking and USMCA/FTA/exemption reductions) on FIXED 2024 consumption-import weights. Our current counterpart is the ex-post collections rate on CONTEMPORANEOUS weights; the constructs differ on both axes, and the fixed-vs-contemporaneous gap is mechanical (imports of high-tariff goods contract, so a fixed-base statutory rate sits above a contemporaneous collections rate). Same-construct replication (our rates x fixed 2024 weights) is the planned stage-1 counterpart.

annotations.text: The tracker publishes daily; scorecard rows are unweighted monthly means of daily values (n_days per row).

Canada rows place Yale's effective statutory rate on fixed 2024 Canada import weights next to Microcosm's observed calculated duties divided by contemporaneous Canada customs value. Yale models product-level USMCA utilization and other statutory adjustments; the observed collections series reflects claims, exclusions, entry timing, compliance, and the contemporaneous trade mix. The delta is therefore a construct comparison, not an apples-to-apples validation and not evidence of Axiom whole-basket coverage.

annotations.text: The spring-2026 divergence between the two fixed-base statutory series is the weight year, quantified by replication: running Yale's own daily-series stage and own rate panel (c4307e51, built locally) with the weight base rebuilt via Yale's own weights recipe for 2025 instead of 2024 moves the 2026-04..06 mean from 10.72% to 9.38%, within 0.08 points of TPC's published 9.46% (weight-year effect -1.34p; construct residual ~0). Author-attributed; leg outputs committed at data/pe/diagnostics/daily_overall_weights{2024,2025}.csv. The validation leg (2024 weights) tracks Yale's published series within 0.2-0.6p in stable months, with departures explained by vintage (their 2026-06-09 publication predates their Brazil-301/338 encodings) and by single-pass vs per-revision weight keying.

annotations.text: TPC's average STATUTORY tariff rate uses FIXED 2025 import-volume weights and EXCLUDES AD/CVD; MFN base rates sit inside the 'Other' type. Our current counterpart is the ex-post collections rate on contemporaneous weights, which includes AD/CVD collections and reflects import contraction; the constructs are not directly comparable. Same-construct replication (our rates x fixed 2025 weights, ex-AD/CVD) is the planned stage-1 counterpart and requires an AD/CVD exclusion list consistent with theirs.
